title: Jimmy Cricket, light-hearted comedy icon, dies at 80
subtitle: British humorist, famous for the catchphrase “And there’s more!”, leaves a legacy of clean, family-friendly comedy.
excerpt: Jimmy Cricket, known for his innocent humor and the catchphrase “And there’s more!”, died at 80, leaving a legacy of light, profanity-free comedy.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The world of comedy lost, this Monday, one of its most beloved representatives: Jimmy Cricket, the British humorist who delighted generations with his unpretentious, vulgarity-free style. At 80, the artist – whose real name is James Joseph Mulg… – passed away, leaving a void in television and family-entertainment stages.

Career start in holiday camps

Jimmy Cricket began his trajectory in the so-called “holiday camps” of northern England, places where British families spent vacations filled with recreational activities. It was in these informal settings that the future comedian learned to interact with audiences, testing jokes that did not rely on profanity or sexualized content. The experience in these camps shaped his brand of humor: direct, gentle and accessible to all ages.

Rise on 1980s television

During the 1980s, Jimmy Cricket gained a foothold on British television, presenting programmes that became reference points for family entertainment. His humor was marked by everyday situations, simple visual gags – such as swapped rain boots or funny hats – and, above all, a tone that avoided “smut” (sexual content) and “swearing” (profanity). This stance set him apart at a time when comedy often resorted to exaggeration and offensive language.

One of the most recognizable elements of his performance was the catchphrase “And there’s more!”, which appeared at the end of each number, signalling that more surprises awaited the audience. This phrasing, besides creating a comic expectation, became a cultural landmark, repeated on radio shows, television and even internet memes.

International recognition

Although his fame was predominantly British, Jimmy Cricket received recognition beyond the United Kingdom’s borders. In 2015, the humorist was honoured with an award bestowed by the Pope, a gesture that symbolised the Catholic Church’s appreciation for his work, which, according to authorities, promoted “joy without offense”. The papal acknowledgement reinforced Jimmy Cricket’s image as an artist who, over decades, maintained a firm commitment to clean, inclusive comedy.

Legacy and influence

The death of Jimmy Cricket arrives at a moment when the debate over the limits of humour is intensifying. His career demonstrates that it is possible to build a successful path without resorting to offensive language or controversial content. Young comedians have cited his example as inspiration to develop a style that prioritises collective laughter, without excluding any segment of the audience.

Beyond television, the artist also left his mark on theatre stages and live events, always retaining the same light-hearted energy that defined him. His humour, often described as “gentle”, managed to cross generational barriers, pleasing both children and adults.

Farewell and reflections

The news of his death was confirmed by sources close to the family, who requested privacy during the mourning period. While fans await tributes and retrospectives, the media and fellow professionals have already begun reflecting on the importance of preserving the tradition of comedy that, like Jimmy Cricket’s, privileges empathy and fun without verbal aggression.

In a landscape where humour frequently polarises, Jimmy Cricket’s trajectory serves as a reminder that laughter can be, above all, a tool for unity. His legacy will remain in television archives, in the memories of those who watched him, and, above all, in the words he immortalised: “And there’s more!”.

With information from The Guardian.
